about-us.title: About Us
about-us.bodyHtml:
TOTTOMS

Our Story

Who we are.

Tottoms started out as a simple idea: make something we would want to use ourselves. It didn’t begin with the goal of selling a product. It started with the desire to create something we were confident riding and standing behind, and that’s where our motto comes from: “By Riders, For Riders.”

It began with three brothers and a close friend who all shared a deep love for this incredible hobby. That passion was shared with millions of people through our social media channels, and along the way, we realized we wanted to do more. We wanted to share our passion with the rest of the world and give people the opportunity to ride the same things we were using ourselves. That’s when Tottoms truly started, giving people access to the same products we trusted, and building a genuine community around drift karting.

Tragically, during the early stages of our mission to build a community-driven business, our brother Bren passed away. While his loss changed everything, it also gave us the motivation to keep his shared dream alive and to make him proud. Bren always put quality and aesthetics above all else, and his vision continues to drive every decision we make as we move forward.

We continue to push ourselves to deliver the best possible products to our supporters. We’re grateful to everyone who has joined us on this journey, because this is only the beginning.

— The Tottoms Team

warranty-shipping-returns.title: Warranty, Shipping, & Returns
warranty-shipping-returns.bodyHtml:
Warranty, Shipping, & Returns

Returns

We have a 7-day return policy, which means you have 7 days after receiving your item to request a return. 

To be eligible for a return, your item must be in the same condition that you received it, unworn or unused, with tags, and in its original packaging. You’ll also need the receipt or proof of purchase.

To start a return, or if you have any questions regarding returns, you can contact us at support@tottoms.com.
If your return is accepted, we’ll send you more information regarding your return.

Damages and issues

Please inspect your order upon reception and contact us immediately if the item is defective, damaged or if you receive the wrong item, so that we can evaluate the issue and make it right.

Refunds

We will notify you once we’ve received and inspected your return, and let you know if the refund was approved or not. If approved, you’ll be automatically refunded on your original payment method within 10 business days. Please remember it can take some time for your bank or credit card company to process and post the refund too.
If more than 15 business days have passed since we’ve approved your return, please contact us at support@tottoms.com.

 



   

Warranty Information

At Tottoms, we stand behind the quality of our products and are pleased to offer the following warranties:

Warranty Terms for PRO and LITE Forks

1. Coverage Period

  • PRO Forks: Limited Lifetime Warranty – Tottoms warrants that PRO Forks shall be free from manufacturing defects for the product’s entire life. (For example: if a weld fails, then we will attempt to repair or replace.)
  • Pre-Built Kart Warranty - Warranty covers powertrain components such as motor, esc, battery or manufacturer defects for 6 months. This does not cover negligence as in water damage.

2. Coverage Scope

  • This warranty covers structural issues including bending or breaking that are a direct result of manufacturing defects.
  • If the product fails due to a manufacturing defect, customers can return it for inspection. Based on the results, Tottoms will provide repair or replacement at its discretion.

3. Exclusions

  • Rust Exclusion: Warranty coverage does not extend to rust for RAW (non-powder-coated) forks. Additionally, Tottoms does not offer powder-coating services for RAW forks after purchase.
  • Customer-Induced Damage: The warranty does not cover damage caused by improper use, handling, or maintenance, including but not limited to scratches or other cosmetic damages resulting from customer actions.

4. Warranty Claims

  • To initiate a warranty claim, please provide proof of purchase and details regarding the issue. All claims are subject to Tottoms’ discretion and may require product inspection.

    6-Month Warranty on Powertrain Parts

    We provide a 6-month warranty on all powertrain parts, including the ESC (Electronic Speed Controller), motor, and battery, under the following conditions:

    • The powertrain warranty is valid only if you are using the complete system provided by Tottoms.
    • If you are using your own battery or any other powertrain parts not provided by Tottoms, the warranty will not be applicable.

    Water Damage Exclusion

    Please note that our warranty does not cover any products that have been water damaged. This includes riding in the rain or through wet areas. Ensure that you keep your Crazy Cart upgrades dry to maintain warranty coverage.

    Warranty Claim Process

    To make a warranty claim, please follow these steps:

    1. Contact Us: Reach out to our customer service team with your order details and a description of the issue.
    2. Return the Parts: Send the parts back to us for inspection. We will evaluate the parts to determine if they are eligible for warranty coverage.
    3. Inspection and Decision: Once we receive the parts, our team will inspect them and inform you of our decision regarding the warranty claim.

    We are committed to ensuring your satisfaction and will work diligently to address any issues covered under our warranty.

    For any questions or further assistance, please contact our customer service team at support@tottoms.com.

     



     

    Release of Liability

    By purchasing and using products from Tottoms, you agree to the following terms and conditions:

    Acknowledgment of Risk

    You acknowledge that the use of Crazy Carts and related upgrades, including but not limited to modifications made by Tottoms, involves inherent risks that may result in injury or damage. These risks include but are not limited to falls, collisions, loss of control, and other accidents.

    Assumption of Risk

    You voluntarily and knowingly assume all risks associated with the use of our products, whether such risks are known or unknown, anticipated or unanticipated.

    Release of Liability

    To the fullest extent permitted by law, Tottoms, its owners, employees, and affiliates shall not be liable for any injuries, damages, or losses sustained while using our products. This includes, but is not limited to:

    • Injuries resulting from falls, collisions, or loss of control.
    • Damages to property or other third parties.
    • Any other risks or hazards related to the use of Crazy Carts and Tottoms upgrades.

    Indemnification

    You agree to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tottoms, its owners, employees, and affiliates from any claims, demands, actions, or causes of action, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of or related to your use of our products.

    No Warranty on Safety

    While our products are designed to enhance your Crazy Cart experience, we do not provide any warranty or guarantee regarding the safety or suitability of our products for any particular use. It is your responsibility to ensure that you use our products safely and in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations.

    Compliance with Laws

    You agree to use our products in compliance with all local, state, and federal laws and regulations. Tottoms shall not be responsible for any violations of law resulting from the use of our products.

    By using our products, you acknowledge that you have read, understood, and agree to be bound by this release of liability. If you do not agree to these terms, do not use our products.

    For any questions or further assistance, please contact our customer service team at support@tottoms.com. 

     



      

    Lithium-Ion Battery Safety and Liability

    Safety Precautions

    The use of lithium-ion batteries requires adherence to safety guidelines to prevent accidents, injuries, and damage. Please follow these important safety precautions when using and charging your lithium-ion batteries:

    1. Always Supervise Charging: Never leave your lithium-ion battery unattended while it is charging. Always keep the battery in sight during the charging process.
    2. Remove for Charging: If you cannot supervise the battery while it is charging, we recommend removing the battery from the Crazy Cart and charging it separately in a safe location.
    3. Use the Correct Charger: Only use the charger provided by Tottoms or one that is specifically designed for your lithium-ion battery. Using an incorrect charger can result in overheating, fire, or explosion.
    4. Charge in a Safe Environment: Charge your battery in a dry, well-ventilated area away from flammable materials. Do not charge the battery in extreme temperatures or in direct sunlight.
    5. Inspect Regularly: Regularly check the battery for any signs of damage, swelling, or leakage. Do not use or charge a damaged battery.
    6. Follow Manufacturer's Instructions: Always follow the manufacturer's instructions and guidelines for the safe use and handling of lithium-ion batteries.
    7. No Tampering: Any signs of tampering with the battery will void the warranty. Do not attempt to disassemble, modify, or repair the battery yourself.

    Release of Liability

    By using Tottoms products, including lithium-ion batteries, you agree to the following terms and conditions:

    1. Assumption of Risk: You acknowledge and assume all risks associated with the use and charging of lithium-ion batteries, including but not limited to fire, explosion, or injury.
    2. Release of Liability: To the fullest extent permitted by law, Tottoms, its owners, employees, and affiliates shall not be liable for any injuries, damages, or losses sustained as a result of using or charging lithium-ion batteries. This includes, but is not limited to:
      • Injuries or damages resulting from battery fires or explosions.
      • Property damage caused by battery malfunctions.
      • Any other incidents related to the use and charging of lithium-ion batteries.
    3. Indemnification: You agree to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tottoms, its owners, employees, and affiliates from any claims, demands, actions, or causes of action, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of or related to the use or charging of lithium-ion batteries.

    By using our lithium-ion batteries, you acknowledge that you have read, understood, and agree to be bound by these safety precautions and the release of liability. If you do not agree to these terms, do not use our lithium-ion batteries.

    For any questions or further assistance, please contact our customer service team at support@tottoms.com.

Sweepstakes Rules

1. Eligibility

  • Open to legal residents of the 50 United States, the District of Columbia, and Canada, excluding Puerto Rico, Quebec, U.S. territories, and where prohibited by law.
  • Entrants must be 18 years or older. Minors under 18 may enter with parental or legal guardian consent. If a minor is selected as the winner, the prize will be awarded to their parent or legal guardian on their behalf, who must fulfill all prize claim requirements.
  • Employees of Tottoms LLC, its affiliates, and their immediate family members are not eligible to enter.

2. Sweepstakes Period

  • The Sweepstakes begins on November 1, 2024, at 12:00 PM (EST) and ends on November 31, 2024, at 11:59 PM (EST).

3. How to Enter

  • Purchase Method: For every $1 spent on Tottoms.com, participants receive 10 entries. Certain products may include bonus entries; please see individual product listings for specific entry details.

  • No-Purchase Method: To enter without purchase, participants may send a handwritten letter to the following address:

    Tottoms LLC 850 East Lime Street PO Box 11 Tarpon Springs, FL 34689

    Each letter must include the phrase "Entering Tottoms Sweepstakes #1," the entrant's full name, address, phone number, and email. Each letter counts as one entry, with a maximum of 20 entries per person. All mailed entries must be postmarked by November 31, 2024, and received by Tottoms LLC within seven (7) days of the Sweepstakes end date to be valid. No mechanically reproduced or bulk entries will be accepted.

4. Entry Limitations

  • Each participant may enter up to 20 times via the no-purchase mail-in method. There are no limits on entries via the purchase method, subject to product availability.

5. Prize Details

  • Prize: A custom-built drift kart & Cash Prize, with an approximate retail value (ARV) of $4,500.
  • The prize is non-transferable and cannot be exchanged for cash or substituted for any other item.

6. Winner Selection and Notification

  • A random drawing will be conducted by Tottoms LLC within 1-7 days of the Sweepstakes end date from all eligible entries received.
  • The potential winner will be notified by email, phone, or both. The winner must respond within 7 days of notification or the prize will be forfeited, and an alternate winner may be selected.

7. Prize Delivery

  • The prize will be shipped via ground shipping or delivered in person within 10 days of the winner's confirmation. Tottoms LLC will cover shipping costs if ground shipping is used.

8. Publicity Release

  • By accepting the prize, the winner grants Tottoms LLC permission to use their name, likeness, and image for promotional purposes on the Tottoms website and associated media channels without additional compensation.

9. General Conditions

  • Tottoms LLC reserves the right to cancel, suspend, or modify the Sweepstakes if technical issues or fraud compromise the integrity of the Sweepstakes.
  • All entries become the property of Tottoms LLC and will not be acknowledged or returned.

10. Release of Liability

  • By participating, entrants agree to release and hold harmless Tottoms LLC, its officers, employees, and affiliates from any and all liability or injuries, losses, or damages arising from participation in the Sweepstakes or the acceptance, possession, use, or misuse of any prize.

11. Fraud Prevention and Disqualification

  • Any attempt to gain entries by fraudulent means, such as returning items purchased solely to acquire entries, will result in disqualification and may result in the participant being barred from future promotions.

12. Dispute Resolution

  • All disputes will be resolved under Florida law, without regard to its conflicts of laws principles. Entrants agree to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, with all claims heard individually.

13. Return Policy for Sweepstakes Purchases

  • Digital Products: Digital products, including Instant Entry Packs, are non-returnable.
  • Physical Products: Physical products may be returned within 7 days of receipt if they are unused and unopened. Contact customer support for return authorization and instructions. Returns made with the intent to exploit entry bonuses will result in disqualification from the Sweepstakes.

14. Contact Information

  • For questions about the Sweepstakes, please contact:
    • Email: support@tottoms.com
    • Phone: 727-494-4652

15. Non-Endorsement Statement

  • This Sweepstakes is in no way sponsored, endorsed, or administered by, or associated with any social media platform or third-party service, including Instagram or Facebook.

motor-detection-guide.title: Motor Detection Guide
motor-detection-guide.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Full VESC Setup Guide with ChargedUp

Our full VESC tuning guide to run you through your entire motor setup.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play
ChargedUp Motor Specifications:

7070 Motors:

Motor type : Generic/Large Outrunner
Motor poles : 14
Temp sensor type : 10k NTC

XL motor:

Motor type : Generic/Large Inrunner Motor poles : 10
Common gearing: 20-22/55
Temp sensor type KTY 83

V3 motor:

Motor type : Generic/Large Inrunner
Motor poles : 6
Common gearing: 16/55
Temp sensor type: KTY 83

What do I set for Battery Cell Series?
  1. Use your charger’s OUTPUT voltage to determine your cell series.
  • Look at the OUTPUT voltage displayed on your charger.
  • Match that number to the correct cell series in the chart below.
  1. Voltage → Cell Series Chart:
  • ~42.0V → 10s
  • ~46.2V → 11s
  • ~50.4V → 12s
  • ~54.6V → 13s
  • ~58.8V → 14s
  • ~63.0V → 15s
  • ~67.2V → 16s
  • ~71.4V → 17s
  • ~75.6V → 18s
  • ~79.8V → 19s
  • ~84.0V → 20s
Battery Current Max:

This is the maximum current(A or Amps) your battery can output. To find this value check your battery specifications for a value called Continuous Discharge Rate. For budget lithium ion batteries, this value is around 20-30a. For Amorge and OnlyAmps batteries this can be 60-80a.

This is an important figure. If it is set wrong, you may experience battery cutout. (cuts all power to cart to protect battery)

Battery Current Regen Max:

This is the maximum current(A or Amps) that your battery can regen at or input back into the battery. Please check with your battery specifications on Max Charge Rate.

If you cannot find this value, check the charge rate of your wall charger. This value usually ranges around 2.5a-5a.

This means you can set your Battery Current Regen Max to the same as your charger.

MAKE SURE YOU SET IT TO NEGATIVE VALUES WITHIN VESC

What is my gearing?

Within VESC, you are able to set your Motor Pulley Tooth Count and your Wheel Pulley Tooth Count.

This will make sure your kart is reading the proper speed.

To find these metrics, count the teeth on your motor sprocket and your wheel sprocket and set accordingly within the app.

Find our written guide below.

Step 1 — Connect to Your VESC

  1. Turn OFF all other VESCs nearby.
     This prevents the app from connecting to the wrong one.
  2. Power ON your kart / VESC.
  3. Open the VESC Tool App.
     (Download links are at the top of the guide.)
  4. Tap CONNECT in the app and select your VESC.

Step 2 — Enter Motor Setup

  1. Once connected, go to the Start tab in the VESC Tool app.
  2. Tap Setup Motors to begin the motor configuration process.
  3. If your kart isn’t running correctly or you want to start fresh, you can tap YES to Load Default Parameters.
  • This will restore the VESC to factory defaults.
  • You’ll need to redo throttle calibration later in the guide.

Step 3 — Motor Type

  1. Click “Generic” and hit Next.
     For Crazy Carts, this is always the correct choice on the first motor-type screen.
  2. Choose the correct motor type (Large Inrunner or Large Outrunner).
     Use the following for ChargedUp motors:
  • ChargedUp 7070 (4000w) — Large Outrunner
  • ChargedUp V3 (6000w) — Large Inrunner
  • ChargedUp XL (7000w) — Large Inrunner
     (If using a different motor, check that motor’s spec sheet.)

Step 4 — Battery Type & Selecting the Correct Cell Series

  1. Verify Battery Type is set to BATTERY_TYPE_LIION_3_0_4_2.
     The VESC Tool automatically selects this battery type by default.
    Stock Crazy Carts use lead-acid, but most upgraded batteries are lithium-ion, which is what this guide is based on.
    Make sure your battery is actually lithium-ion before continuing.
  2. Use your charger’s OUTPUT voltage to determine your cell series.
  • Look at the OUTPUT voltage displayed on your charger.
  • Match that number to the correct cell series in the chart below.
  1. Voltage → Cell Series Chart:
  • ~42.0V → 10s
  • ~46.2V → 11s
  • ~50.4V → 12s
  • ~54.6V → 13s
  • ~58.8V → 14s
  • ~63.0V → 15s
  • ~67.2V → 16s
  • ~71.4V → 17s
  • ~75.6V → 18s
  • ~79.8V → 19s
  • ~84.0V → 20s
  1. Enter your battery’s capacity (Ah).
     This value is printed on your battery or listed on its spec sheet.

Step 5 — Advanced Battery Settings (Battery Current Max & Regen)

  1. Check the “Advanced” box to unlock battery current settings.
  2. Set Battery Current Regen.
  • Start with 0A to -5A.
  • Check your battery’s spec sheet for a safe charge/regen limit if you want to increase it.
  • Do not exceed your battery’s safe charging current.
  1. Set Battery Current Max.
  • Look up your battery’s continuous discharge rating (from the label or spec sheet).
  • Set Battery Current Max 5–10 amps lower than that number to avoid BMS cutoff.
    (Example: A 40A continuous battery → set 30–35A.)
  1. Click Next to continue.

Step 6 — Gear Ratio, Motor Poles & Temp Sensor Settings

  1. Enter your gear ratio.
  • Motor Pulley: tooth count on your motor sprocket
  • Wheel Pulley: tooth count on your wheel sprocket
  • Wheel Diameter: Stock Crazy Cart wheel is 203 mm
     (Use your actual numbers if you’ve changed sprockets.)
  1. Enter your motor’s pole count.
     Use the correct value for your motor:
  • ChargedUp 7070 (4000w) — 14 poles
  • ChargedUp V3 (6000w) — 6 poles
  • ChargedUp XL (7000w) — 10 poles
    (Check your motor’s spec sheet if using a different motor.)
  1. Select the correct temp sensor type.
  • ChargedUp 7070 (4000w) — NTC 10k @ 25°C
  • ChargedUp V3 (6000w) — KTY84
  • ChargedUp XL (7000w) — KTY84

Step 7 — Motor Detection (IMPORTANT: Lift the Kart!)

  1. Lift the front of the kart off the ground.
     The wheel will spin at high speed during detection.
    Make sure the kart is secure and nothing is touching the wheel.
  2. Click “Run Detection.”
  • The motor will spin up to ~25–50% speed.
  • Then it will slow down to detect the hall sensors.
  1. Wait for the “Success” message.
     If it does not say success, detection must be redone.
  2. Check your detection values.
  • Temp Comp = TRUE
  • Sensors = Hall Sensor
  • If it says Sensorless, hall detection failed.
  1. Click “OK”
  2. Press FWD to verify motor direction.
  • If the wheel spins backward, enable Inverted.
  • If it spins forward correctly, leave Inverted OFF.
  1. Click Finish once the motor spins correctly.

Step 8 — Throttle Calibration (ADC Input Setup)

  1. Go to the Start tab and tap Setup Input.
  2. Wait for it to reconnect to your VESC.
  3. Click Next until you reach the Input Setup screen.
  4. Select ADC Input.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Press the throttle a few times, then fully release it.
  • Note: The bar may not go all the way to the end yet — this is normal.
  1. Tap Apply & Write.
  2. Press the throttle again.
  • This time, the throttle bar should reach the full range.

  1. Click Next to continue.

  2. Disable Safe Start.
     Safe Start causes issues on Crazy Carts and should be OFF.
  3. Keep Control Type: Current
  • Only change this if you’re setting up regen braking (covered later).
  1. Click Write Configuration to save the settings.

Step 9 — Motor Configuration (Motor Amps, Absolute Max, Battery Current Check)

  1. Scroll to the Motor CFG tab at the top of the VESC Tool App.
  2. There are two “General” tabs in this section.
    Change the second General tab to “Current” mode.
  3. Set Motor Current Max.
  • Recommended range: 90–120A
  • Important rule:
  • Do not exceed 3× your Battery Current Max.
    (Example: If your battery is set to 30A, don’t go above 90A motor amps.)
  1. Set Motor Current Max Brake to the same value as Motor Current Max.
  2. Set Absolute Maximum Current.
  • Recommended range: 250–400A
  • If your motor cuts out under heavy load (ex: burnouts), increase slightly.
  • Never exceed 400A.
  1. Make sure Slow ABS Current Limit is checked.
  2. Scroll down to Battery Current Max and confirm:
  • It does NOT exceed your battery’s safe continuous discharge rating.
  • This should match the value you set earlier.
  1. Check Battery Current Regen and confirm it’s within your battery’s safe charging/regen limits.
  2. Tap Write to save all settings.
    (Nothing is saved unless you press Write.)

Step 10 — Final Checks & Next Steps

  1. Double-check all settings were saved.
  • Look for the blue confirmation bar after each Write.
  • If you didn’t tap Write, the settings did not save.
  1. Power-cycle your kart.
     Turn the kart off, then back on to ensure everything loads correctly.
  2. Test the throttle on the stand first.
  • Make sure the motor spins smoothly.
  • Make sure direction is correct.
  • Listen for grinding, stuttering, or weak/noisy startup (could indicate wiring issues).
  1. Do a slow parking-lot test.
  • Light throttle → smooth acceleration
  • Full throttle → no cutouts
  • Coast → no weird surges
  • Hard acceleration → no thermal faults or dropouts

We recommend using our custom ChargedUp User Interface! Check out the link below to make tuning even easier!

ChargedUpAPP Back to Resources

Step 2 — Navigate to Hall Sensor Detection

  1. Scroll to the Motor CFG tab at the top of the app.
  2. Tap the three dots in the bottom-right corner.
  3. Select “Detect FOC Hall Sensors.”

Step 3 — Run the Hall Sensor Detection

  1. Lift the front of the kart off the ground —
    The wheel will spin during detection.
  2. Tap Detect.
  3. Wait for the Hall Table to appear.
  • If it says Detection Failed, common causes include:
  • Bad hall sensor wire
  • Damaged or loose connector
  • Bent pins
  • Wrong motor type selected
  1. Tap Apply and Close.

Tap WRITE to save the settings.(Nothing saves unless you press Write.)

throttle-calibration-guide.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Throttle Calibration Guide with ChargedUp

Our guide to fix weak and inconsistent throttle.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play

Throttle Calibration Guide (ADC Input Setup)

Step 1 — Connect to Your Kart

  1. Turn OFF all other VESCs nearby.
     Prevents the app from connecting to the wrong one.
  2. Power ON your kart / VESC.
  3. Open the VESC Tool App and tap CONNECT.

Step 2 — Enter Input Setup

  1. Go to the Start tab.
  2. Tap Setup Input.
  3. Wait for it to reconnect to your VESC.
  4. Tap Next until you reach the Input Setup screen.
  5. Select ADC Input.
  6. Tap Next.

Step 3 — Calibrate the Throttle

  1. Press the throttle a few times, then fully release it.
  • The bar may NOT reach full range yet — this is normal before saving.
  1. Tap Apply & Write.
  2. Press the throttle again.
  • This time, the bar should move through the full range.
  1. Tap Next to continue.

Step 4 — Final Input Settings

  1. Disable Safe Start.
     Safe Start causes issues on Crazy Carts and should be OFF.
  2. Make sure Control Type = Current.
     (Only change this if you're setting up regen braking later.)
  3. Tap Write Configuration to save the settings.
    (Nothing saves unless you press Write.)
Back to Resources

restore-firmware-guide.title: Restore Firmware Guide
restore-firmware-guide.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Firmware Restore Guide with ChargedUp

Our guide for restoring your 75v100 v2 back to version 6.00.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play

Firmware Update Guide (Recommended: Version 6.00)

Best Firmware for Crazy Carts — Smoothest Performance & Most Stable Version

Step 1 — Open Firmware Update Menu

  1. Go to the Start tab in the VESC Tool App.
  2. On the left side, scroll down and tap Update Firmware.

Step 2 — Download the Firmware Archive

  1. At the top of the screen, scroll the horizontal bar to Archive.
  2. Tap Update Archive to download all firmware versions.
  3. This download may take 5–10 minutes depending on your phone and internet speed.

Step 3 — Select Firmware Version 6.00

  1. Once the archive finishes downloading, tap the Firmware Version Box.
  2. Change the firmware version to v6.00.
  3. Why 6.00?
  • Best stability
  • Best motor detection behavior
  • Most reliable for Crazy Cart performance
  • Avoids issues seen in later 6.x firmware changes

Step 4 — Upload the Firmware

  1. Tap Upload (bottom-left of the screen).
  2. The firmware upload process will take 5–10 minutes.
  3. When finished, you will likely need to reconnect to your VESC.

Step 5 — Verify Firmware Version

  1. Return to the Update Firmware tab.
  2. Scroll back to Archive.
  3. At the bottom of the screen, confirm that FW = v6.00.
  4. If it displays v6.00, you are fully updated.

⚠ IMPORTANT — Firmware Resets Your Entire Controller

Updating firmware wipes your controller settings.

You must redo the following:

  • Motor Setup
  • Hall Sensor Detection
  • Throttle Calibration
  • Battery Settings
  • Motor Current Settings
  • Regen Braking Setup (if used)

Setup Guide Back to Resources

off-throttle-regen.title: Step 1 — Connect to Your VESC
off-throttle-regen.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Off Throttle Regen Braking Guide with ChargedUp

Our guide to setup off throttle regen braking.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play

Regen Braking Setup Guide (ADC Input — Off-Throttle Regen)

Throttle Calibration Guide + Motor Setup Guide REQUIRED Before Doing This

⚠ READ THIS FIRST

Regen braking uses Battery Current Regen Max Amps.

If this value is NOT set correctly in Motor CFG, you can:

  • Trigger BMS Shutdown
  • Cut throttle mid-ride
  • Damage your battery

If you are not sure, please see the Motor Setup Guide first.

Step 1 — Connect to Your VESC

  1. Turn ON your kart / VESC.
  2. Open the VESC Tool App.
  3. Tap CONNECT and select your VESC.

Step 2 — Switch to ADC Control Mode

  1. Scroll the top bar to App CFG.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Change App to Use → ADC.
  4. Change Control Type → Current No Reverse Brake Center.

What this means:

  • The throttle’s “center point” determines when regen activates.
  • By default, regen begins at half throttle on the return stroke — we will fix that in the next step.

Step 3 — Adjust Regen Activation Point

To make regen activate immediately when you release throttle, adjust the center:

  1. Under the ADC area, there is another General box.
  2. Tap this box → select Mapping.

You will now see two important values:

  • ADC1 Start Voltage
  • ADC1 Center Voltage

Recommended Setting

Set ADC1 Center Voltage to 0.10V above ADC1 Start Voltage.

Example:

  • Start Voltage: 0.90V
  • Center Voltage: 1.00V

This ensures regen activates instantly off-throttle, not halfway.

  1. Tap Write — settings will not apply unless you write them.

Step 4 — Set Regen Strength Using Profiles

Regen braking force is controlled by motor current scaling inside Profiles.

  1. Scroll to the Profiles tab (top bar).
  2. Tap Add Profile.
  3. Adjust Motor Current Scale → start with 5–15%.

    This percentage determines regen braking intensity.

    You can increase or decrease based on preference.
  4. Tap Save Profile.
  5. Tap Use Permanently.

    (If you don’t, the profile will reset when reconnecting.)

Step 5 — Confirm Battery Regen Limits (IMPORTANT)

Regen is only as safe as your battery’s regen capability.

Go to: Motor CFG → General (Current mode)

Check Battery Current Regen Max.

Recommended Value

  • -5A is safe for most lithium-ion packs.

If you are unsure:

👉 Refer to the Motor Setup Guide (Battery Settings section).

Motor Setup Guide Back to Resources

separate-throttle-regen.title: Step 1 — Identify the Correct Connectors
separate-throttle-regen.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Separate Throttle Regen Braking Guide with ChargedUp

Our guide to setup regen braking with two throttles or a thumb throttle.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play

Regen Brake Setup (Separate Pedal or Thumb Throttle)

Requires ChargedUp Regen Brake Cable — Separate Input for ADC2

⚠ Required Hardware

To use a separate brake pedal or thumb throttle for regen braking, you must use this cable:

👉 ChargedUp Regen Brake Cable:

https://chargedup3d.com/products/75100-v2-regen-brake-cable

This cable splits the throttle input into two ADC channels (ADC1 = throttle, ADC2 = regen brake).

Step 1 — Identify the Correct Connectors

The regen brake cable has two throttle connectors:

Connector 1 — Regular Throttle (ADC1)

  • Wires: Black / White / Red
  • This connects to your main throttle pedal on the kart.

Connector 2 — Regen Brake Throttle (ADC2)

  • Wires: Contains BLUE wire
  • The one with the blue wire is your regen throttle input (ADC2).
  • This connects to your separate brake pedal or thumb throttle.

Make sure both connectors are plugged in properly before continuing.

Step 2 — Connect to Your VESC

  1. Turn ON your kart / VESC.
  2. Open the VESC Tool App.
  3. Tap CONNECT to connect to your VESC.

Step 3 — Enter Input Setup

  1. Go to the Start tab.
  2. Tap Setup Input.
  3. When prompted, choose ADC Input.

You should now see two bars on the screen:

  • Top Bar → ADC1 (Throttle Pedal)
  • Bottom Bar → ADC2 (Regen Brake Throttle)

Step 4 — Calibrate Both Throttles

  1. Press your main throttle a few times → release it.
  2. Press your regen brake throttle a few times → release it.
  3. Tap Apply & Write.
  4. Press both throttles again to confirm the bars fill their full range.
  5. Tap Next.

Step 5 — Set Control Type for Two-Throttle Operation

  1. Change Control Type to:

    Current No Reverse Brake ADC2

    ADC1 = main throttle

    ADC2 = regen brake pedal / thumb throttle
  2. Disable Safe Start.
  3. Tap Write Configuration.
  4. Tap Next.

Step 6 — Set Regen Braking Strength (Profiles Tab)

Regen braking force is controlled through motor scaling:

  1. Scroll to the Profiles tab.
  2. Tap Add Profile.
  3. Set Motor Current Scale to 5–15% to start.
    Higher % = stronger regen braking

    Start low to avoid overly aggressive braking
  4. Save the profile.
  5. Tap Use Permanently so the regen profile stays active.

Step 7 — Verify Battery Regen Safety Limits

Battery Current Regen Max MUST be set correctly or you can damage your battery.

Go to:

Motor CFG → General (Current Mode)

Check:


  • Battery Current Regen Max = ~ -5A (safe for most packs)

If unsure:

👉 Refer to the Motor Setup Guide

Motor Setup Guide Back to Resources

vesc-app.title: VESC App
vesc-app.bodyHtml:
Back

⚡Install the ChargedUp VESC App

Use the ChargedUp App to make tuning easier than ever.

VESC APP REQUIRED FOR THIS GUIDE

You can find the app for your mobile device below.

Download on the App Store
Get it on Google Play
ChargedUp APP Download
ChargedUp Motor Specifications:

7070 Motors:

Motor type : Generic/Large Outrunner
Motor poles : 14
Temp sensor type : 10k NTC

XL motor:

Motor type : Generic/Large Inrunner Motor poles : 10
Common gearing: 20-22/55
Temp sensor type KTY 83

V3 motor:

Motor type : Generic/Large Inrunner
Motor poles : 6
Common gearing: 16/55
Temp sensor type: KTY 83

Battery Current Max:

This is the maximum current(A or Amps) your battery can output. To find this value check your battery specifications for a value called Continuous Discharge Rate. For budget lithium ion batteries, this value is around 20-30a. For Amorge and OnlyAmps batteries this can be 60-80a.

This is an important figure. If it is set wrong, you may experience battery cutout. (cuts all power to cart to protect battery)

Battery Current Regen Max:

This is the maximum current(A or Amps) that your battery can regen at or input back into the battery. Please check with your battery specifications on Max Charge Rate.

If you cannot find this value, check the charge rate of your wall charger. This value usually ranges around 2.5a-5a.

This means you can set your Battery Current Regen Max to the same as your charger.

MAKE SURE YOU SET IT TO NEGATIVE VALUES WITHIN VESC

What is my gearing?

Within VESC, you are able to set your Motor Pulley Tooth Count and your Wheel Pulley Tooth Count.

This will make sure your kart is reading the proper speed.

To find these metrics, count the teeth on your motor sprocket and your wheel sprocket and set accordingly within the app.

VESC Package Install & ChargedUp3D UI Guide

Step 1 — What This Package Does

The ChargedUp3D VESC Package installs a custom tab inside VESC Tool that makes adjusting:

  • Battery cell series
  • Battery amps
  • Motor amps
  • Power settings

MUCH easier and faster than using default VESC menus.

Great for beginners and advanced riders.

Step 2 — Connect to Your Kart

  1. Turn OFF all other VESCs nearby.

    Prevents connecting to the wrong controller.
  2. Power ON your kart / VESC.
  3. Open the VESC Tool App.
  4. Tap CONNECT and select your VESC.

Step 3 — Download the Correct Package File

  1. Download the package file from the video description.
  2. This package is specific to the 75v100 v2 VESC Controller.

    (Do NOT use on other controllers.)

Download Link:

ChargedUpApp

Step 4 — Install the Package

  1. Inside VESC Tool, go to Package Store.
  2. Tap the three dots (top-right).
  3. Select Install From File.
  4. Choose the file you downloaded.
  5. Tap Open.

    Install time: ~10 seconds
  6. Tap Close when done.
  7. Wait a moment.

You should now see a new tab at the top labeled:

App UI (ChargedUp3D UI)

This confirms installation was successful.

Step 5 — Using the ChargedUp3D UI

Battery Series

  1. Find the Battery Series section.
  2. Match this to your charger output voltage.

10s — 42.0v

11s — 46.2v

12s — 50.4v

13s — 54.6v

14s — 58.8v

15s — 63.0v

16s — 67.2v

17s — 71.4v

18s — 75.6v

19s — 79.8v

20s — 84.0v

*So if your charger output voltage is 67.2v set your cell series to 16s and so on.*

Battery Amps

  1. Set battery amps slightly lower than your battery’s continuous discharge rating.
  2. This prevents BMS cutouts during hard acceleration.

Example:

60A BMS → set battery amps to 50-55A.

Motor Amps

  1. Recommended starting point: 90A.

    (150A is extremely twitchy.)

Automatic Motor Amp Limiting

The ChargedUp UI will automatically cap Motor Amps so they never exceed:

Motor Amps ≤ 3× Battery Amps

This protects your battery, BMS, controller, and motor.

Apply Settings

  1. Once all your values are set, tap:

    Apply Power Settings
  2. This instantly updates motor/battery current settings.

To verify:

Motor CFG → Current tab

Your new numbers will be shown there.

This makes power tuning faster, safer, and much easier.

Back to Resources

adjustable-seat-install-guide.title: Adjustable Seat Install Guide
adjustable-seat-install-guide.bodyHtml:
Adjustable Seat Install Guide

Follow these simple steps to get started. Click images to enlarge.

1

Tools Needed

You will need:

M4 Allen Key

M5 Allen Key

M6 Allen Key

2

REMOVE SEATBELT

Seatbelt is included but not recommended for Crazy Cart use. Please remove seatbelt and reinstall bolts. Seatbelt will not be needed.

16:9 Image
3

Remove Stock Seat

Grab your M5 allen key and remove 4 bolts holding on the stock seat.

4

Gather Adapter Plate & Hardware

You will need:

The metal adapter palte

6 M6 countersunk bolts

6 metal spacers

5

Grab 6 Metal Spacers

You will need these for the next step.

6

Put Spacers Over The Rear 6 Holes

Carefully put the spacers over the 6 holes with arrows above them.

7

Put Spacers Here

Do not put the spacers over the area with the red X's. Only put the spacers over the areas with arrows.

8

Place Adapter Plate On Spacers

Carefully place the plate on top of the spacers without moving the spacers.

9

Verify Spacers are Unmoved

Check that the spacers have not shifted and are directly underneath the holes.

10

Gather 6 Countersunk Screws

You will need these for the next step

11

Insert 6 Screws In Countersunk Holes

Insert the screws inside of the countersunk holes with arrows listed.

12

Tighten Screws

Verify that the screws are tightened securely.

13

Grab 4 Small Washers

These 4 washers will be placed under the rails.

14

Place 4 Washers Over The M8 Holes

Very important to place these small washers over the M8 holes for proper rail movement.

15

Remember to place all 4 washers

Place 4 washers in these positions located here.

16

Gather Shorter Rails and 4 Small Screws

Grab the parts shown in the image.

VERIFY THAT YOU ARE USING THE SHORTER RAILS.

(THE OTHER RAILS ARE FOR THE SEAT)

17

Place Rails on Plate ON TOP OF WASHERS

Verify that the rail with teeth is on the side listed in the picture.

18

Line Up Holes With Plate

Make sure that the rail with the teeth is on the left side of the kart and that the holes are lined up with the plate.

(MAKE SURE TEETH ARE FACING OUT)

19

Grab 4 Small Screws

Gather the smaller screws shown in the image.

20

Bolt Down Rails to Plate

Place 4 screws in holes and secure rails to adapter plate.

21

Gather 4 Bolts and Taller Rails

Verify that you are using the rails with the handle and the other rail that looks similar along with the 4 bolts.

22

Get Your Seat

Grab your seat from the package.

23

Flip Seat Over

Find the 4 holes underneath the bottom of the seat.

24

Place Rails on Seat

Place rail with handle on the left side of the seat. And place the other rail without the handle on the right side of the seat over the holes.

25

Grab 4 Bolts

Gather the 4 bolts for bolting the rails onto the seat.

26

Put 4 Bolts into Holes

Line rails with holes and securley fasten the rail sytstem.

27

Line Up Rails

Line up the seat rails with the rails on the kart and insert carefully.

28

Pull Handle on Seat and Slide in

Pull handle on left side of the seat and slide in until it clicks.

29

You're Done!

Enjoy the adjustability and cushion of your new seat. Thank you!
